findings.title: Telehealth settled at a steady base, it did not disappear
findings.text: National use peaked at 46.7% in 2020-Q2. Since 2023 it has held between 10.8% and 14.8% a quarter, and was 12.7% in 2026-Q1 (-1.1 pts vs 2024-Q1), about 2.7 million people. The low point since 2020 was 10.8% in 2025-Q4.
findings.so_what: Plan virtual capacity as a permanent, steady share of visits rather than a pandemic surge that is still unwinding.

findings.title: Where a patient lives changes telehealth use by more than 4x
findings.text: In 2026-Q1, California led at 21.9% and Mississippi was lowest at 5.0%. Only 16 of 51 states (incl. DC) beat the national rate. Highest: California, Massachusetts, District of Columbia, New York, Minnesota. Lowest: Mississippi, Alabama, Iowa, Nebraska, Idaho.
findings.so_what: Benchmark virtual share against your own state, not the national average, before setting targets.

findings.title: Rural patients use telehealth less than urban patients
findings.text: Nationally 9.9% of rural vs 13.5% of urban eligible users had a telehealth service in 2026-Q1. Rural use was lower in 37 of 50 states with both groups reported (DC has no rural ZIP codes); the widest gap was Minnesota (13.7% rural vs 19.1% urban).
findings.so_what: Rural outreach needs more than a video link: audio-only options, broadband help and scheduling support are where the gap can close.

findings.title: Under-65 beneficiaries with disabilities are the heaviest users
findings.text: Beneficiaries under 65 (Medicare through disability or ESRD) used telehealth at 26.9%, 2.2x the 65-74 rate (12.1%). Use edges down with age: 11.0% at 75-84 and 10.9% at 85+. By entitlement, Disabled 27.3%, ESRD 19.9%, Aged 11.4%.
findings.so_what: Protect virtual access for patients with disabilities and ESRD first; they would feel any policy rollback most.

findings.title: Dual-eligible (low-income) beneficiaries use telehealth 2.1x as often as Medicare-only
findings.text: Dual-eligible (Medicare & Medicaid) beneficiaries used telehealth at 22.8% vs 10.9% for Medicare-only, higher in 51 of 51 states. By race/ethnicity, Hispanic beneficiaries were highest at 16.1% and American Indian/Alaska Native lowest at 11.8% (Non-Hispanic White 12.1%).
findings.so_what: Track virtual share by payer and demographic group in clinic dashboards; a cut to telehealth falls hardest on dual-eligible patients.
